# TESTING_GUIDE — Runner catalogue bug (TDD examples)

Task: `b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c`  
Companion to `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` + `REPLICATION_GUIDE.md`. This guide gives concrete **test examples** you can copy into the repo to drive the structural fix test-first. All examples are **illustrative** — file paths and import names match the current codebase but may need minor adjustment when you wire them up.

> Safety note: every test below runs in-memory with fakes. **DO NOT** extend them to spawn the real `muse`/`pi`/`codex` CLIs, hit prod endpoints, or start real Runners/Agents without explicit user permission — see `REPLICATION_GUIDE.md` “flagged” table.

---

## How to run

```bash
npm test -- runner/harnessModelDiscovery.test.js
npm test -- runner/modelDiscovery.test.js
npm test -- api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.test.js
```

New tests can live alongside those files (e.g. `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.repro.test.js` for repro, then promote to permanent tests). Delete repro-only files once the fix lands.

---

## 1) Keep-old cache must expire (cause 1)

### Goal
Stale/dummy ids that are never reconfirmed should not live forever. A TTL + eviction replaces indefinite keep-old.

### Example — stale slice evicted after TTL

```js
// runner/harnessModelDiscovery.ttl.test.js
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach } from "vitest";
import { discoveryCache, clearDiscoveryCache, runDiscoveryLeg } from "./harnessModelDiscovery.js";

describe("discovery TTL eviction (structural fix)", () => {
  beforeEach(() => clearDiscoveryCache());

  it("evicts a stale slice that has not been reconfirmed within TTL", async () => {
    const TTL_MS = 24 * 3600 * 1000;
    // seed a dummy id as if a prior round returned it
    discoveryCache["pi"] = {
      ids: ["pi::test::dummy-model"],
      atMs: Date.now() - (TTL_MS + 1000), // stale
      error: null,
    };

    // next leg fails (timeout) — with the fix, stale slice is evicted, not kept
    const res = await runDiscoveryLeg("pi", {
      discoverFn: async () => { throw Object.assign(new Error("timeout"), { code: "ETIMEDOUT" }); },
      ttlMs: TTL_MS,
    });

    expect(res.ids).toEqual([]); // evicted, not kept
    expect(res.error?.code).toBe("STALE_EVICTED");
  });

  it("keeps a fresh slice on transient failure within TTL", async () => {
    const TTL_MS = 24 * 3600 * 1000;
    discoveryCache["pi"] = {
      ids: ["pi::mistral::real-model"],
      atMs: Date.now() - 1000, // fresh
      error: null,
    };
    const res = await runDiscoveryLeg("pi", {
      discoverFn: async () => { throw new Error("transient"); },
      ttlMs: TTL_MS,
    });
    expect(res.ids).toEqual(["pi::mistral::real-model"]);
  });
});
```

### Example — new model appears after successful round

```js
it("replaces cache with new ids when a later round succeeds (muse-ember appears)", async () => {
  clearDiscoveryCache();
  discoveryCache["muse"] = { ids: ["muse::meta::old-model"], atMs: Date.now(), error: null };

  const res = await runDiscoveryLeg("muse", {
    discoverFn: async () => ["muse::meta::muse-ember", "muse::meta::old-model"],
  });
  expect(res.ids).toContain("muse::meta::muse-ember");
});
```

---

## 2) Allowlist must not silently shadow discovery (cause 2)

### Goal
`operatorConfig.availableModels` should not be the sole truth. Divergence must be observable.

### Example — quarantine diverges from allowlist

```js
// api/flow/dispatch/effectiveRunnerModels.divergence.test.js
import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
import { effectiveRunnerModels } from "./runnerMatches/effectiveRunnerModels.js";
import { runnerModelConfirmation } from "./runnerModelConfirmation.js";

describe("allowlist vs discovered divergence", () => {
  it("flags an allowlist id that no claimant discovered", () => {
    const runnerId = "r1";
    const discoveredByRunner = ["pi::mistral::real"]; // what the leg actually saw
    const allowlist = ["pi::deepseek::gemma4"];       // what operator asserted

    // effectiveRunnerModels currently returns allowlist alone when set — divergence hidden
    const advertised = effectiveRunnerModels({ operatorConfig: { availableModels: allowlist } }, discoveredByRunner);
    // desired after fix: advertised still serves allowlist, but confirmation marks it stale
    const verdict = runnerModelConfirmation({
      modelId: "pi::deepseek::gemma4",
      runnerId,
      discoveredByRunnerIds: discoveredByRunner,
      isOperatorAsserted: true,
    });
    // operator-asserted ids are currently "unknown" (trusted) — after fix, optionally warn
    expect(advertised).toContain("pi::deepseek::gemma4");
    // add assertion for new divergence signal, e.g. verdict.divergent === true
  });
});
```

> TDD note: the first assertion already passes today; the divergence signal (`verdict.divergent` or `staleAdvertReason`) is the new behaviour to add (Layer B).

## 3) Grammar gate — single `:` ok, `::` rejected, siblings not dropped (cause 3)

### Goal

### Example — muse leg with mixed ids

```js
// runner/modelDiscovery.colon.test.js

import { discoverClaudeModels } from "./modelDiscovery.js";

describe("muse leg grammar", () => {
  it("keeps single-colon ids and skips double-colon ids without dropping siblings", async () => {

      strict: false,

      "muse::meta::muse-ember:cloud",

    expect(ids).not.toContain("muse::meta::bad::model");
  });
});
```

### Example — catalogue ingest quarantine (Layer C)

```js
  });
});
```

## 4) Runner count, not “unavailable” flag, is the UX truth (cause 4)

### Goal
Picker rows show `N runners` / `0 runners` rather than a blocking “Unavailable” badge.

### Example — snapshot retention then eviction (Layer C)

```js
// api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.retention.test.js
import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
import { createFleetModelSnapshotStore } from "./fleetModelSnapshot.js";

describe("fleet snapshot retention", () => {
  it("keeps a dropped model as 0 runners for the retention window, then evicts it", () => {
    const RETENTION_MS = 14 * 24 * 3600 * 1000;
    const store = createFleetModelSnapshotStore({ filePath: null, retentionMs: RETENTION_MS });

        capabilities: { harnesses: [{id:"pi"}], models: ["pi::mistral::m1","pi::mistral::m2"], tiers: [] } }
    ]);
    expect(store.getSnapshot().models.find(m => m.id === "pi::mistral::m2").available).toBe(true);

    // 2) runner stops serving m2 — it becomes 0 runners but stays visible
    store.update([
      { status: "active", runnerId: "r1",
        capabilities: { harnesses: [{id:"pi"}], models: ["pi::mistral::m1"], tiers: [] } }
    ]);
    expect(store.getSnapshot().models.find(m => m.id === "pi::mistral::m2").runnerCount).toBe(0);
    // after fix: available derived from runnerCount, retention window not yet elapsed so entry still present
    expect(store.getSnapshot().models.find(m => m.id === "pi::mistral::m2")).toBeDefined();

    // 3) after retention elapsed, entry is evicted (simulate by advancing lastSeenAtMs)
    // (requires injecting clock or mutating snapshot test seam — adapt to actual API)
  });
});
```

```js
import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
import { createFleetModelSnapshotStore } from "./fleetModelSnapshot.js";
import { buildFleetModelCatalog } from "./fleetModelCatalog.js";

describe("end-to-end: discovery → heartbeat → catalogue → snapshot", () => {
```

## 1) Keep-old cache must expire (cause 1)

### Goal
Stale/dummy ids that are never reconfirmed should not live forever. A TTL + eviction replaces indefinite keep-old.

### Example — stale slice evicted after TTL

```js
// runner/harnessModelDiscovery.ttl.test.js
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach } from "vitest";
import { discoveryCache, clearDiscoveryCache, runDiscoveryLeg } from "./harnessModelDiscovery.js";

describe("discovery TTL eviction (structural fix)", () => {
  beforeEach(() => clearDiscoveryCache());

  it("evicts a stale slice that has not been reconfirmed within TTL", async () => {
    const TTL_MS = 24 * 3600 * 1000;
    // seed a dummy id as if a prior round returned it
    discoveryCache["pi"] = {
      ids: ["pi::test::dummy-model"],
      atMs: Date.now() - (TTL_MS + 1000), // stale
      error: null,
    };

    // next leg fails (timeout) — with the fix, stale slice is evicted, not kept
    const res = await runDiscoveryLeg("pi", {
      discoverFn: async () => { throw Object.assign(new Error("timeout"), { code: "ETIMEDOUT" }); },
      ttlMs: TTL_MS,
    });

    expect(res.ids).toEqual([]); // evicted, not kept
    expect(res.error?.code).toBe("STALE_EVICTED");
  });

  it("keeps a fresh slice on transient failure within TTL", async () => {
    const TTL_MS = 24 * 3600 * 1000;
    discoveryCache["pi"] = {
      ids: ["pi::mistral::real-model"],
      atMs: Date.now() - 1000, // fresh
      error: null,
    };
    const res = await runDiscoveryLeg("pi", {
      discoverFn: async () => { throw new Error("transient"); },
      ttlMs: TTL_MS,
    });
    expect(res.ids).toEqual(["pi::mistral::real-model"]);
  });
});
```

### Example — new model appears after successful round

```js
it("replaces cache with new ids when a later round succeeds (muse-ember appears)", async () => {
  clearDiscoveryCache();
  discoveryCache["muse"] = { ids: ["muse::meta::old-model"], atMs: Date.now(), error: null };

  const res = await runDiscoveryLeg("muse", {
    discoverFn: async () => ["muse::meta::muse-ember", "muse::meta::old-model"],
  });
  expect(res.ids).toContain("muse::meta::muse-ember");
});
```

1|# RESPONSE — Runners are not correctly creating a catalogue
2|
3|Task: `b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c`
4|Stage: response (docs-only). Inputs: bug report + `assets/image.png`, `SURVEY.md` (round 1), `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` (answered round), `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md`, `REPLICATION_GUIDE.md`, `TESTING_GUIDE.md`, plus a read-only look at the live engine state on this host (`~/.kainbain/engine/*.json`, running processes) and the code on this branch.
5|
6|This file does three things:
7|
8|1. Says which candidate causes in `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` are worth fixing, and adds causes found in live state that the earlier analysis missed (§2).
9|2. Gives a way to confirm the bug today, with no code changes (§3).
10|3. Splits the fix into work packages (WP-A … WP-G). It says which ones can run in parallel and which ones block others, and gives each one its own way to confirm the bug and verify the fix (§4–§6).
11|
12|---
13|
14|## 1. TL;DR
15|
16|The screenshot is explained by **five concrete defects that compound**. Four of them can be proven from live state on this host:
17|
18|| # | Symptom in the screenshot | Proven cause (live evidence) |
19||---|---|---|
20|| 1 | `muse-ember` missing | Both local runners (`local-alpha`, `local-bravo`) advertise a **hand-pinned list** (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS` in `~/.kainbain/runner-local-*.env`), report `modelSource: "pinned"` and `discoveryStatus: {}`. **Model discovery has never recorded a single result on them.** The runner process runs straight out of the engine's own git checkout (`/home/[REDACTED]/projects/kainbain/runner`), which KainBain switches between branches. The file on disk was replaced **4 s after the runner booted** with an older daemon that skips discovery whenever models are pinned. `runner/version.json` has said `0.1.0` since 2026‑10‑31, so no runner can tell that it runs stale code, and the self-updater never sees a newer version. This is why "many tickets fixed it" yet nothing changed. |
21|| 2 | `gemma4:31b-cloud` under an `OLLAMA-CLOUD-DIRECT` section in the **Muse** picker (and `deepseek-v4-flash:0731-cloud`) | The pin list includes ids that are **not harness-qualified** (`ollama-cloud-direct::gemma4:31b-cloud` is provider-form, `deepseek-v4-flash:0731-cloud` is bare). `catalogIngest` stamps every entry with **the runner's whole harness list** (`['antigravity','muse','pi','vibe']`) rather than the harness named in the id. `fleetModelsForHarness` then lets provider/bare ids into every section. |
22|| 3 | `test-fleet-model` shown as `Unavailable` | It comes from the API test suite (`api/routes/projects.alias.test.js`, `projects.modelCombination.test.js`). Those tests register runner `test-fleet-muse` against the **live** `~/.kainbain/engine/runners.json` and `fleet-catalog.json`, because neither the global test setup nor these files isolate `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_STATE_FILE` / `KAINBAIN_FLEET_CATALOG_FILE`. The snapshot never deletes entries, so the dummy row stays forever. |
23|| 4 | Old `Unavailable` badge rather than "N runners" | `ModelSelector.jsx` lets `fleetSnapshotBadgeNode` (the "Unavailable" verdict) win over `fleetCountBadgeNode`. The **harness** row ("Muse Code UNAVAILABLE") comes from the *backend container's* local CLI probe (`harnessAvailabilityBadgeNode` → backend `harnessDiscovery`), not from the fleet. The backend container has no `muse` binary, even though runners serve Muse. |
24|| 5 | Pinned models show "1 runner" even though nothing has ever verified them | `confirmRunnerModel` returns `unknown` (counted as serving) for pins when no discovery result exists, and it always does so for provider/bare-form ids. The user wants pins to be **unverified / 0 runners** (survey q3/q4/q12). |
25|
26|There is a sixth, secondary defect. `server2-alpha`'s pi discovery leg fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND '@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent'`. Runner discovery legs lazily `import()` backend harness modules and their npm dependencies (`runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js:374,455,504,656`), and the runner install does not ship them. As a result, that runner advertises 0 models and all of its entries drift to `Unavailable`.
27|
28|**The structural fix:** make the runner's *real, versioned code* do the discovery (A, B); accept only `harness::provider::model[::effort]` ids into the catalogue, with counts based on verification (C); render counts, never stored flags (D); and stop tests and ops from polluting live state (E, F).
29|
30|---
31|
32|## 2. Assessment of candidate causes
33|
34|### 2.1 Causes from `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md`
35|
36|| WIDE_NET cause | Verdict | Reasoning |
37||---|---|---|
38|| **1. Keep-previous-slice cache / snapshot never deletes** | **Partially valid, re-scoped.** | *Runner side:* keep-old is **not** what hides `muse-ember` today, because on the local runners no slice has ever been written (`discoveryStatus: {}`). A bounded staleness marker is still wanted (survey q5: "keep up to a time limit, then mark stale"), so it goes into WP-B as a small item. *Backend side:* "keep with 0 runners indefinitely" is **what the user explicitly wants** (RESPONSE_SURVEY q1), so the proposed backend TTL/retention eviction is **rejected**. It is replaced by an admin "remove permanently" action (q1 note) and by dropping the size cap (q6). |
39|| **2. Operator allowlist (`availableModels`) trusted as servable** | **Valid in principle, but not the live trigger.** | Every runner in `runners.json` has `operatorConfig.availableModels: null`. The live trigger is the same *pattern* through a different door: the runner-side pin (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS`). Both doors get the same treatment in WP-C: declared ≠ verified (q3/q4). |
40|| **3. Grammar/filter mismatch across legs** | **Re-framed.** | The single-`:` colon issue was already fixed by `9d2b75a2`. The real grammar defect is that **non-harness-qualified ids (bare / provider-form) are accepted at all**, and then fanned out to every harness the runner serves. The user's note on q8 ("this should all be based around the `harness::model::effort` ids so it shouldn't be possible") and q7 ("block them from being saved at all") make the fix a strict canonical-id contract at ingest (WP-C) and at the runner's config (WP-B). |
41|| **4. Dual presentation contract (`available` flag vs runner count)** | **Valid.** | Confirmed in `ModelSelector.jsx:318-342`: the snapshot verdict wins over the count badge. The harness badge is also backend-local. Fixed in WP-D, with a small contract addition in WP-C. |
42|
43|### 2.2 New causes (not in WIDE_NET), with evidence
44|
45|| New cause | Evidence (read-only, this host, 2026‑11‑13 ~17:20Z) | Package |
46||---|---|---|
47|| **N1. Runners execute mutable, unversioned code.** | The `local-bravo` process (`pid 256984`, started `2026‑11‑12 11:51:20`) has cwd `/home/[REDACTED]/projects/kainbain/runner`, which is the engine's project checkout (currently on branch `kb/b3401f19…`). `runner/daemon.js` and `runner/modelDiscovery.js` in that checkout have mtime `11:51:24`, 4 s *after* boot. `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js` **does not exist** there, and the on-disk `refreshDiscoveredModels` returns early when `config.models` is pinned. `runner/version.json` = `0.1.0`, last changed `2026‑10‑31`. All runners report `versions.runner: "0.1.0"`. | WP-A, WP-F |
48|| **N2. Discovery has never produced a result on pinned local runners.** | `runners.json`: `local-alpha` / `local-bravo` → `modelSource: "pinned"`, `discoveryStatus: {}`, `modelProvenance: {}`; 17 models, all equal to the env pin. | WP-B (+A, F) |
49|| **N3. Runner discovery legs depend on backend modules and npm deps the runner install lacks.** | `server2-alpha.discoveryStatus.pi.error = ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND '@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent' … /runner/api/agent/harnesses/pi/piHarness.js`; `muse: MUSE_MSP_MODELS_EMPTY`. | WP-B |

Catalogue entries inherit the runner's full harness list.** | `fleet-catalog.json`: every `local-alpha` entry has `harnesses: ['antigravity','muse','pi','vibe']`, including `ollama-cloud-direct::gemma4:31b-cloud` (form `provider`) and `deepseek-v4-flash:0731-cloud` (form `bare`). Code: `catalogIngest.js:101` (`harnesses: cleanStringList(ctx?.harnesses)`) and `fleetModelSnapshot.js:213-224`. | WP-C |

API tests write to live engine state.** | `fleet-catalog.json` contains `muse::meta::test-fleet-model` with provenance `test-fleet-muse`. `runners.json` contains revoked runner `test-fleet-muse`. `api/testSetup.isolation.js` sets neither `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_STATE_FILE` nor `KAINBAIN_FLEET_CATALOG_FILE`. `api/isolatedTestRoots.js` sets the runner/claims/steer files but **not** the fleet catalogue, and the two offending test files use neither helper. | WP-E (+F cleanup) |
52|| **N6. Harness badge is the backend container's local probe.** | Screenshot: "Muse Code UNAVAILABLE" plus the hint "Install the Muse CLI…" (text from `api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js:610`). The backend runs in a container (`pid 256006`, cwd `/app`). `ModelSelector.jsx:33-44` derives the badge from the backend's discovery projection. | WP-C (contract) + WP-D |

Read text file `docs/tasks/b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c/WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md`.
1|# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS — Runner catalogue creation bug
2|
3|Task: `b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c`  
4|Stage: investigation + replication & structural fix proposal (docs-only)  
5|Inputs: bug report (`assets/image.png`), `SURVEY.md`, task spec, plus repo history and prior tickets (notably `9d2b75a2-1ecd-47ce-a9f9-b3068c5f5cf7`).
6|
7|## Scope
8|
9|This report is investigatory. It proposes possible *causes* of the runner catalogue defect, assesses replicability/testability, and proposes the shape of a structural long-term fix. No code is changed in this stage.
10|
11|The reported symptoms are:
12|
13|- newly released harness models (e.g. `muse-ember`) never appear;
14|- dummy/test models appear in production catalogue views;
15|- broken harness models from other harnesses appear in places they should not (e.g. `gemma4`, `deepseek`);
16|- models that are available are still shown with the old “unavailable” flag instead of “how many runners serve it”;
17|- repeated backend/runner restarts and prior tickets did not durably correct it.
18|
19|The intended flow is:
20|
21|```
22|runner harness scan → discoveredModelsCache → heartbeat facts.models
23|  → runnerRegistry capabilities → fleet snapshot (/runners/models/catalogue)
24|  → frontend withFleetModels / fleetCountBadgeNode
25|```
26|
27|## Evidence base
28|
29|- `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js` (discovery legs, cache slicing, validation)
30|- `runner/modelDiscovery.js` (`discoverClaudeModels`, `resolveAdvertisedModels`)
31|- `runner/daemon.js` (`refreshDiscoveredModels`, `factsFor`, keep-old behaviour)
32|- `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js` (`heartbeat`, persisted `_persist`, capabilities)
33|- `api/flow/dispatch/normalizeCapabilities.js`
34|- `api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.js` / `fleetModelCatalog.js`
35|- `api/flow/dispatch/runnerModelConfirmation.js`
36|- `frontend/src/services/fleetModelOptions/*`, `frontend/src/services/modelStatus.js`
37|- Prior ticket root cause: `docs/tasks/9d2b75a2-1ecd-47ce-a9f9-b3068c5f5cf7/ROOT_CAUSE.md`
38|
39|---
40|
41|## Candidate cause 1 — “keep previous slice” cache semantics create sticky stale/dummy ids and hide brand-new models
42|
43|### Summary
44|
45|Discovery on each leg is deliberately non-destructive: `runDiscoveryLeg` keeps the *previous* per-harness slice on failure, empty result, unparseable output, or grammar-invalid incoming ids. `refreshDiscoveredModels` then keeps the global `discoveredModelsCache` when the combined round is empty. Persisted backend `fleetModelSnapshot.js` additionally keeps stale entries as *unavailable* rather than deleting them.
46|
47|### Why this could be the bug
48|
49|- Pros:
50|  - A transient scan failure can never erase a known-good menu, so operators reasonably see old models “forever” after a bad scan.
51|  - A scan that once returned a dummy id (mock/test model, stale manual pin) is retained unless a later round replaces it; the UI therefore still shows it in catalogue views.
52|  - New models (e.g. `muse-ember`) only appear when the *next successful* round both succeeds and validates them; empty/failed rounds leave the previous cache, so release cadence alone cannot clear the gap.
53|  - Backend side: `fleetModelSnapshot.update` only flips previously available-but-now-unserved entries to unavailable; it never deletes them, so old ids remain in `/runners/models/catalogue` as `Unavailable` instead of being replaced by live `runnerCount` entries. This matches the observed “old unavailable flag”.
54|- Cons / counter-evidence:
55|  - The design intentionally keeps history (survey round 1 answer notes users *want* dropped models to remain visible with `0 runners`), so “keep but mark unavailable” is partly desired behaviour, not purely a defect.
56|  - The cache is replaceable when a round succeeds (`combinedIds.length > 0`), so a healthy runner *should* eventually refresh it; sticky staleness requires a continuous scan failure or cache desync.
57|- References:
58|  - `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js` — `runDiscoveryLeg` (keep previous on empty/invalid/failure), `runDiscoveryRound`
59|  - `runner/daemon.js` — `refreshDiscoveredModels` (`if (combinedIds.length > 0) { discoveredModelsCache = combinedIds; }`)
60|  - `api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.js` — `update()` marks non-live entries `available: false` instead of deleting
61|  - `docs/tasks/9d2b.../ROOT_CAUSE.md` — suspect (d) pin-wins + TTL cadence; suspect corridor “empty round keeps cache”
62|
63|### Replicability
64|
65|Replicable without prod. See `REPLICATION_GUIDE.md` §1 and `TESTING_GUIDE.md` §1. Unit-testable by seeding `discoveryCache` with a dummy id, simulating a failed/empty leg, and asserting the dummy survives.
66|
67|---
68|
69|## Candidate cause 2 — Operator allowlist (`availableModels`) replaces the advertised list and is trusted as servable
70|
71|### Summary
72|
73|`effectiveRunnerModels` uses `operatorConfig.availableModels` instead of `runner-reported` models whenever set. `confirmRunnerModel` always marks operator-asserted ids as `unknown` (trusted) so they become available even when no discovery slice listed them. The backend persisted runner records (and local state file) also retain the allowlist independently of heartbeats.
74|
75|### Why this could be the bug
76|
77|- Pros:
78|  - A stale or hand-entered allowlist can expose ids that no harness currently serves (including dummy/test, `gemma4`, `deepseek`) because `effectiveRunnerModels` no longer consults the scanned menu.
79|  - Operator assertions are never contradicted by the runner’s own discovery, so they ride through fleet snapshot ingestion and appear in the catalogue as valid entries with non-zero runner counts.
80|  - Conversely, a stale allowlist can hide newly discovered models when it does not include them (or when discovery is disabled with `modelDiscoveryIntervalMs: 0`), so new releases are omitted.
81|  - Persisted `runners.json` / `lastSeenAt = null` after backend restart means old capability lists or allowlists can survive in a degraded form, and the fleet snapshot can continue carrying entries until heartbeats overwrite it.
82|- Cons / counter-evidence:
83|  - This behaviour is by design: it exists to let operators serve models an under-reporting runner cannot discover.
84|  - The allowlist is operator-provided, not runner-generated; if the reported dummy models are truly “test models”, some other mechanism must seed them.
85|- References:
86|  - `api/flow/dispatch/runnerMatches/effectiveRunnerModels.js`
87|  - `api/flow/dispatch/runnerModelConfirmation.js` — operator-asserted ids trust rule
88|  - `api/flow/runnerRegistry.js` — `normalizeOperatorConfig`, `availableModels`, persisted state (`_loadState`/`_persist`)
89|  - `docs/tasks/9d2b.../ROOT_CAUSE.md` — suspect (g) operator allowlist shadow
90|
91|### Replicability
92|
93|Replicable without prod. Set `availableModels: ["deepseek::deepseek::fake", "muse::meta::dummy"]` on a runner, heartbeat, and observe catalogue. See `REPLICATION_GUIDE.md` §2.
94|
95|---
96|
97|## Candidate cause 3 — Grammar/filtering mismatches across legs drop valid new models and leak invalid ones
98|
99|### Summary
100|
101|Different parts of the chain apply different validity rules to model ids:
102|
103|- runner muse leg (`runner/modelDiscovery.js`) previously rejected any provider/model containing `:` — now fixed to reject only `::` but other legs still differ in edge cases;
104|- backend MSP parser (`api/agent/harnesses/muse/msp/...`) does not filter `:` ;
105|- shared grammar allows single `:` in ids;
106|- several backend transforms (`shared/modelKeys.js:withModelKey`) throw on `::`, which can discard a whole agy/vibe result set;
107|- frontend `fleetModelsForHarness` creates synthesized entries from snapshot ids without re-validating against the backend harness section.
108|
109|### Why this could be the bug
110|
111|- Pros:
112|  - A newly released model whose provider/model id contains `:` (common for cloud-tagged models) can be dropped by one leg while other paths retain it, so the runner never pushes it to the catalogue. The reverse mismatch can make a model present in one view but absent elsewhere.
113|  - The muse-vs-rest asymmetry explains why “muse-ember” and models like `gemma4`/`deepseek` drift between harness sections.
114|  - The strict section gate in `fleetModelsForHarness` drops ids when serving harnesses do not include the rendered harness, so a runner that advertises an id for the wrong harness causes silent disappearance.
115|  - Dummy/test models can remain if they are grammatically valid but no longer real (keep-old behaviour compounds this), with no authority to reconcile against live harness menus.
116|- Cons / counter-evidence:
117|  - The filter bug alone does not explain stale *persistence* after the list should update, or the disappearance of the `runnerCount` display focus.
118|  - Backend MSP has no colon filter and therefore already handles `:` correctly, so a pure colon filter only explains runner leg omission, not leakages from backend models.
119|- References:
120|  - `runner/modelDiscovery.js` (`discoverClaudeModels` colon filter — now `::`-only)
121|  - `shared/modelKeys.js` (parse rules, `withModelKey`, throws on `::`)
122|  - `frontend/src/services/fleetModelOptions/fleetModelsForHarness.js` (serving harness gate)
123|  - `docs/tasks/9d2b.../ROOT_CAUSE.md` — suspect (c), section 3 “other-leg audit”
124|
125|### Replicability
126|
127|Replicable without prod. Inject a `muse serve` row with `modelId: "muse-ember:cloud"` and verify leg output. See `REPLICATION_GUIDE.md` §3.
128|
129|---
130|
131|## Candidate cause 4 — Catalogue representation still mixes two presentation contracts (old `unavailable` vs runner-count)
132|
133|### Summary
134|
135|The UI now treats fleet availability as runner count (`fleetCountBadgeNode`) while persisted snapshot entries retain and expose an explicit `available: false` + `unavailableReason`. Components consult `fleetSnapshotBadgeNode` first, so older/cached snapshot rows can badge “Unavailable” even when the count/runner data has changed.
136|
137|### Why this could be the bug
138|
139|- Pros:
140|  - Inconsistent rendering means a model can still display the old unavailable badge in a picker even though its snapshot/counts should now say `N runners`.
141|  - Because the snapshot marks non-live entries unavailable and never removes them, the “old unavailable flag” directly persists as `available: false`, while the count (`runnerCount`) is reset to 0, making a valid current model look unavailable if snapshot refresh is delayed or uses stale runner input.
142|  - This is consistent with the user’s stated requirement: replace “unavailable” with “how many runners have that harness/model available”.
143|- Cons / counter-evidence:
144|  - This is primarily a frontend presentation/reporting issue. It explains display, not necessarily why new models are missing from the underlying catalogue.
145|  - The count badge still renders `0 runners`, so counts are technically shown even when unavailable.
146|- References:
147|  - `frontend/src/services/modelStatus.js` (`fleetSnapshotBadge`, `fleetSnapshotBadgeNode`, `fleetCountBadgeNode`)
148|  - `frontend/src/hooks/useFleetModelCatalog/fleetCountsById.js`
149|  - `api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.js` (`available`, `unavailableReason`, `runnerCount`)
150|  - `SURVEY.md` q3 notes
151|
152|### Replicability
153|
154|Replicable without prod (frontend unit test) and with a snapshot reload (backend restart without heartbeats). See `REPLICATION_GUIDE.md` §4.
155|
156|---
157|
158|## Cross-cutting observations
159|
160|- Multiple historical tickets (see `docs/tasks/9d2b.../ROOT_CAUSE.md`) repeatedly fixed piecewise symptoms (colon filter, stale pins, unavailable badges) but preserved the architectural invariants above. Any one of them failing can reproduce the entire visible defect, which explains why small fixes did not durably resolve it.
161|- The backend and runner use different cadences/caches; structural reconciliation would need a clear invalidation/replacement contract across discovery slices, runner facts, registry capabilities, and persisted fleet snapshots.
162|
163|## Bottom line
164|
165|At least four interacting mechanisms are plausible root causes, and the defect likely involves more than one:
166|
167|1. keep-old cache behaviour retaining stale/dummy models;
168|2. operator allowlists bypassing and contradicting discovery;
169|3. grammar/filter mismatches between discovery, heartbeat, and fleet ingestion;
170|4. mixed `available` vs runner-count presentation with persisted snapshot staleness.
171|
172|These should be examined together in the structural fix.
173|
174|---
175|
176|## Structural long-term fix — proposal (docs-only, not yet implemented)
177|
178|The recurring failure mode is: **no single source of truth and no clear lifecycle** for "which models are real right now". Each layer (leg slice → global cache → heartbeat → registry → fleet snapshot → frontend section) has its own keep-old, trust-allowlists, or mark-unavailable-not-delete rule. Piecewise patches to one layer cannot fix the others. A durable fix needs a structural contract.
179|
180|### Principles
181|
182|1. **One canonical lifecycle:** `discovered → advertised → registered → catalogued → displayed` with explicit TTL/eviction at each step, not implicit keep-old.
183|2. **Provenance everywhere:** every model id carries *who saw it, when, via which leg/harness*, so stale/dummy entries are attributable.
184|3. **No silent keep-old without expiry:** a cached entry that is not reconfirmed within a bounded window is either evicted or demoted to `available: false` with a countdown to deletion, not retained forever.
185|4. **Grammar validated once, at the edge:** normalize/validate at discovery ingestion; downstream layers never re-filter or re-invent validity.
186|5. **Counts, not flags, as primary UX:** frontend renders `runnerCount` as truth; `available/unavailable` is derived, never stored as independent flag.
187|
188|### Recommended shape (4 layers)
189|
190|#### Layer A — Runner discovery: slice TTL + explicit eviction
191|
192|- Each `discoveryCache[harnessId]` entry gets `atMs` + `ttlMs` (e.g. 24 h, configurable via `KAINBAIN_DISCOVERY_TTL_MS`).
193|- `runDiscoveryLeg` on **successful non-empty** round: replaces slice (current behaviour).
194|- `runDiscoveryLeg` on **failure/empty/invalid**: keeps previous slice *but* records `error` and checks TTL. If `now - atMs > ttlMs`, the slice is **evicted** (set to `[]` with `error: STALE_EVICTED`), not kept indefinitely.
195|- `refreshDiscoveredModels` combined cache: same TTL gate. Optionally add a `forceRefresh` heartbeat field so the backend can request re-probe.
196|- Telemetry: expose `getDiscoveryStatus()` with `ageMs`, `ttlMs`, `error` per harness so Settings can show "stale (12 h old, next eviction in 12 h)".
197|
198|#### Layer B — Heartbeat advertisement: pin semantics made explicit
199|
200|- Keep `resolveAdvertisedModels` pin-UNION-discovered default, but:
201|  - Tag each advertised id with source: `pin` vs `discovered` vs `allowlist` (via a parallel `advertisedProvenance` map, not just a string label).
202|  - When `operatorConfig.availableModels` is set, the backend should still **record** the discovery list alongside the allowlist (new field `discoveredModels` in capabilities) so divergence is observable.
203|  - Add an operator warning when allowlist and discovery disagree (e.g. allowlist id not seen in discovery for > TTL).
204|
205|#### Layer C — Backend fleet snapshot: single ingestion point with quarantine and retention policy
206|
207|- Already partially exists (`fleetModelSnapshot.js` quarantine + `FLEET_SNAPSHOT_MAX_MODELS` eviction). Extend:
208|  - **Grammar gate once:** `catalogIngest.js` validates every incoming `facts.models` against `shared/modelKeys.js` grammar. Malformed ids go to `quarantined` with reason, never to `models`.
209|  - **Stale-pin detection:** `runnerModelConfirmation` already exists — keep it, but surface `staleAdvertReason` in snapshot `unavailableReason` so UI can say "advertised by runner X but never discovered by it".
210|  - **Retention policy:** replace "mark unavailable forever" with: mark `available: false` immediately, but evict entries that stay unavailable for `KAINBAIN_FLEET_CATALOG_RETENTION_MS` (e.g. 14 days, to satisfy the "keep dropped models at 0 runners for deprecation" requirement) — configurable, with oldest-unavailable-first eviction when cap exceeded.
211|  - **Restart behaviour:** after backend restart, snapshot reloads as unavailable until heartbeats reconfirm (current), but with visible `lastSeenAtMs` age so UI can show "waiting for runners to re-report (X min ago)".
212|
213|#### Layer D — Frontend: count-first rendering, no dual truth
214|
215|- Frontend `fleetCountsById` + `fleetCountBadgeNode` is already the intended new contract ("how many runners have that harness/model"). Complete the migration:
216|  - Remove any `fleetSnapshotBadgeNode` "Unavailable" badge from picker rows; replace with `N runners` / `0 runners — not currently served` (grey, but not an error badge).
217|  - Quarantined ids never render as selectable options (only in diagnostics/Settings if exposed).
218|  - Stale-pin / retention-warning ids render with a subtle annotation ("advertised but not discovered by runner") not a blocking badge.
219|
220|### Migration checklist
221|
222|- [ ] Add `KAINBAIN_DISCOVERY_TTL_MS` + eviction in `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js` + `runner/daemon.js`.
223|- [ ] Add `KAINBAIN_FLEET_CATALOG_RETENTION_MS` + eviction in `api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.js`.
224|- [ ] Make `catalogIngest` the single grammar gate; remove downstream re-filtering.
225|- [ ] Surface `discoveredModels` alongside `availableModels` in registry; warn on divergence.
226|- [ ] Frontend: retire `fleetSnapshotBadgeNode` "Unavailable" as primary badge in pickers.
227|- [ ] Add persistence tests: backend restart → snapshot → heartbeat reconfirm → eviction.
228|
229|### Why this survives repeated tickets
230|
231|- TTL+eviction bounds staleness even if one leg stays broken.
232|- Single grammar gate prevents per-leg drift.
233|- Provenance makes "where did this dummy id come from?" answerable without guessing.
234|- Retention window satisfies the deprecation-visibility requirement (0 runners) without permanent clutter.
235|- Count-first UX removes the old "unavailable" flag as a source of confusion.
236|
237|---
238|
239|## Replicability & testability summary
240|
241|All four candidate causes are replicable **without touching prod or invoking real agents**. See the companion guides:
242|
243|- `REPLICATION_GUIDE.md` — quick manual replication steps per symptom (all flagged where prod/real-agent invocation would be needed, and not attempted here).
244|- `TESTING_GUIDE.md` — runnable test examples (TDD-style) for each cause, including what needs a harness mock vs a real CLI spawn.
245|
246|If a symptom cannot be reproduced under mock conditions, the guide flags it and describes what a prod-safe reproduction would look like (with explicit permission required).

1|# REPLICATION_GUIDE — Runner catalogue bug
2|
3|Task: `b3401f19-2897-4049-aa3c-227bcee46a4c`  
4|Companion to `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md`. Each section is a self-contained quick guide to reproduce one visible symptom. All steps run locally with mocks/fakes — no prod touch, no real agent invocation. Where a step would need prod or a real external CLI, it is flagged **DO NOT RUN WITHOUT EXPLICIT USER PERMISSION** and a safe alternative is given.
5|
6|> Prereqs: repo checkout, `npm install`. Tests use the existing `runner/daemon.js`, `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js`, `api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.js` seams.
7|
8|---
9|
10|## 1) New model (e.g. `muse-ember`) never appears — stale cache hides it
11|
12|### What you should see
13|A new harness model released today does not appear in the catalogue picker, even after backend/runner restarts.
14|
15|### Likely involved causes
16|WIDE_NET cause 1 (keep-old cache) + cause 2 (allowlist) + cause 3 (grammar filter).
17|
18|### Minimal local repro (no prod, no real CLI)
19|
20|1. Seed a runner discovery cache with an old list:
21|   ```js
22|   // in a test file or node repl with the runner harnessModelDiscovery harness
23|   import { discoveryCache, clearDiscoveryCache, runDiscoveryLeg } from "./runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js";
24|   clearDiscoveryCache();
25|   discoveryCache["muse"] = { ids: ["muse::meta::old-model"], atMs: Date.now(), error: null };
26|   discoveryCache["pi"]    = { ids: ["pi::mistral::old-model"], atMs: Date.now(), error: null };
27|   ```
28|
29|2. Make the next discovery round fail (timeout / missing binary / empty catalogue). Use the harness fake:
30|   ```js
31|   await runDiscoveryLeg("muse", {
32|     discoverFn: async () => { throw Object.assign(new Error("spawn muse ENOENT"), { code: "ENOENT" }); }
33|   });
34|   // discoveryCache.muse should still be ["muse::meta::old-model"]
35|   ```
36|
37|3. Simulate the newly released model that *should* have been discovered:
38|   ```js
39|   const newModelId = "muse::meta::muse-ember"; // or "muse::meta::muse-ember:cloud"
40|   // It is NOT in discoveryCache.muse because the leg kept the old slice.
41|   ```
42|
43|4. Call `refreshDiscoveredModels` with an empty combined round — it keeps the old global cache:
44|   ```js
45|   import { refreshDiscoveredModels } from "./runner/daemon.js";
46|   // after a round where every leg returned [] / kept previous, combinedIds stays old
47|   ```
48|
49|5. Heartbeat the old `facts.models` to the backend, then read `GET /api/runners/models/catalogue` — `muse-ember` is absent.
50|
51|### What proves the fix
52|After adding TTL+eviction (WIDE_NET Layer A), repeat with a stale `atMs` (e.g. `Date.now() - 25*3600*1000`). The old slice should be evicted to `[]` and the next successful round should replace it with the new model.
53|
54|### Flag: needs real CLI?
55|To truly discover `muse-ember` you would need the real `muse serve` binary answering `model/list` with that row. **DO NOT invoke the real CLI against prod credentials without explicit permission.** Use the fake above — it exercises the same keep-old path.
56|
57|---
58|
59|## 2) Dummy/test models appear in prod catalogue, and wrong-harness models leak (e.g. `gemma4`, `deepseek`)
60|
61|### What you should see
62|Picker shows ids that no harness actually serves, or that belong to a different harness.
63|
64|### Likely involved causes
65|Cause 1 (sticky dummy id) + cause 2 (allowlist shadow) + cause 3 (grammar drift).
66|
67|### Minimal local repro A — sticky dummy via keep-old
68|
69|1. Inject a dummy id as if a prior discovery once returned it:
70|   ```js
71|   discoveryCache["pi"] = { ids: ["pi::test::dummy-model", "pi::mistral::real"], atMs: Date.now(), error: null };
72|   ```
73|
74|2. Run a failing leg; observe the dummy survives (keep-old).
75|
76|3. Heartbeat and check `fleetModelSnapshot` — dummy is live-derived and persisted as `available: true`.
77|
78|### Minimal local repro B — allowlist shadow (no discovery needed)
79|
80|1. Register a runner without discovery, but set an operator allowlist:
81|   ```js
82|   // via backend API or directly in runnerRegistry test harness
83|   registry.updateOperatorConfig(runnerId, { availableModels: [
84|     "muse::meta::dummy-test-model",
85|     "pi::deepseek::gemma4",       // wrong harness / fake provider
86|     "muse::deepseek::deepseek-r1" // wrong harness
87|   ]});
88|   ```
89|
90|2. Heartbeat with `facts.models: []` — `effectiveRunnerModels` still advertises the allowlist ids (trusted, `unknown` in `confirmRunnerModel`).
91|
92|3. `fleetModelSnapshot.update()` ingests them as available entries with `runnerCount: 1`.
93|
94|4. Frontend `fleetSectionMerge` / `fleetModelsForHarness` shows them in the wrong sections.
95|
96|### What proves the fix
97|- TTL eviction clears stale dummy ids that are never reconfirmed (Layer A).
98|- Allowlist ids carry provenance `source: "allowlist"` and are warned when not in `discoveredModels` (Layer B).
99|- Malformed ids go to `quarantined` not `models` (Layer C quarantine).
100|
101|---
102|
103|## 3) Grammar mismatch drops `:` models or leaks `::` ids
104|
105|### What you should see
106|A new model id containing `:` (e.g. `muse-ember:cloud`, `glm-4:cloud`) appears in backend MSP but not in runner catalogue, or an id with `::` breaks one leg’s parse and drops valid siblings.
107|
108|### Likely involved cause
109|Cause 3.
110|
111|### Minimal local repro — single `:` should pass, `::` should be rejected
112|
113|1. Fake a `muse serve` stdout that includes both:
114|   ```js
115|   const fakeStdout = [
116|     JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc:"2.0", id:2, result: { models: [
117|       { providerId: "meta", modelId: "muse-ember:cloud" },  // legal single `:`
118|       { providerId: "meta", modelId: "bad::model" },         // illegal `::` — should be skipped
119|       { providerId: "meta", modelId: "muse-ember" }          // plain — should pass
120|     ]}})
121|   ].join("\n");
122|
123|   import { discoverClaudeModels } from "./runner/modelDiscovery.js";
124|   const ids = await discoverClaudeModels({
125|     spawnSyncFn: () => ({ stdout: fakeStdout, error: null, status: 0 }),
126|     strict: false
127|   });
128|   // Expect: ["muse::meta::muse-ember:cloud", "muse::meta::muse-ember"] — no :: entry
129|   ```
130|
131|2. Verify the old bug would have dropped the `:cloud` variant (historical `:` filter). Confirm current code only rejects `::`.
132|
133|3. Also test `shared/modelKeys.js` throw on `::` — wrap `withModelKey("pi::deepseek::bad::model")` in try/catch and assert the whole agy/vibe parse does not abort sibling rows (quarantine vs throw).
134|
135|### Flag
136|No real CLI needed — the fake `spawnSyncFn` is the recommended path. **DO NOT** run the real `muse` CLI with manipulated provider names against prod without permission.
137|
138|---
139|
140|## 4) Old “unavailable” flag instead of runner count
141|
142|### What you should see
143|Picker badges say “Unavailable” (grey/red) instead of “2 runners” / “0 runners”.
144|
145|### Likely involved cause
146|Cause 4 (dual presentation contract) + cause 1 snapshot keep-unavailable.
147|
148|### Minimal local repro — snapshot persistence
149|
150|1. Create a snapshot with two models:
151|   ```js
152|   import { createFleetModelSnapshotStore } from "./api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.js";
153|   const store = createFleetModelSnapshotStore({ filePath: null });
154|   store.update([
155|     { status: "active", runnerId: "r1", capabilities: { harnesses: [{id:"pi"}], models: ["pi::mistral::m1","pi::mistral::m2"], tiers: [] } }
156|   ]);
157|   // Both available, runnerCount 1
158|   ```
159|
160|2. Make `m2` disappear (runner stops serving it):
161|   ```js
162|   store.update([
163|     { status: "active", runnerId: "r1", capabilities: { harnesses: [{id:"pi"}], models: ["pi::mistral::m1"], tiers: [] } }
164|   ]);
165|   // m2 is now { available: false, unavailableReason: "No claim-eligible runner...", runnerCount: 0 }
166|   ```
167|
168|3. Assert frontend `fleetSnapshotBadgeNode(snapshotEntry)` renders "Unavailable" while `fleetCountBadgeNode({runnerCount:0})` would correctly render "0 runners".
169|
170|### What proves the fix
171|Frontend uses `fleetCountBadgeNode` everywhere in pickers; snapshot `available` is derived from `runnerCount > 0` at read, not stored as independent truth (Layer D).
172|
173|---
174|
175|## Running the existing repo tests for these areas
176|
177|```bash
178|# Runner discovery + daemon
179|npm test -- runner/harnessModelDiscovery.test.js
180|npm test -- runner/daemon.test.js
181|
182|# Muse leg colon handling
183|npm test -- runner/modelDiscovery.test.js
184|
185|# Fleet snapshot / catalogue / confirmation
186|npm test -- api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelSnapshot.test.js
187|npm test -- api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelCatalog.test.js
188|npm test -- api/flow/dispatch/runnerModelConfirmation.test.js
189|npm test -- api/flow/dispatch/catalogIngest.test.js
190|
191|# Frontend
192|npm test -- frontend/src/services/fleetModelOptions
193|npm test -- frontend/src/services/modelStatus.test.js
194|```
195|
196|All of the above are safe to run locally without prod or real agent execution.
197|
198|---
199|
200|## What cannot be replicated without real invocation / prod (flagged)
201|
202|| Scenario | Why not mockable | Safe alternative |
203||---|---|---|
204|| Actual `muse serve` answering with `muse-ember` | Requires installed CLI + login + provider auth | Use `spawnSyncFn` fake as in §3 |
205|| Runner on a real host with missing CLI / login | Host-specific error classification (`MUSE_MSP_BIN_MISSING`, `PI_MODELS_EMPTY`) | Unit-test the classifier with fake `spawnError` objects |
206|| Multi-runner fleet aggregation with real heartbeats | Needs live runners + backend + `/runners/models/catalogue` polling | Use `createFleetModelSnapshotStore({filePath:null})` in a test with synthetic runner records |
207|| Persisted `fleet-catalog.json` surviving a backend restart | Requires filesystem + restart cycle | Test `normalizeSnapshotState` + file round-trip with a temp file; delete after |
208|
209|**DO NOT** attempt any of the right-hand “real” variants on a prod host, with prod credentials, or by invoking live agents/Runners against prod, without explicit user permission. The mocked paths above exercise the same code branches.

45|the change list, survey constraints (q1/q3–q13 round 1; q15–q24 round 2, incl. q15 warn-only,
46|q18 harness-attribution reconciliation, q23 no agent-initiated runner restarts), acceptance
47|criteria, and sequencing (E/A/B/C/D parallel, D merges after C, F blocked on A+B+C+E, G gated on F).
48|
49|## Sequencing for operators
50|
51|1. Start WP-E first (prevents re-pollution), WP-A/B/C/D in parallel.
52|2. Merge WP-D only after WP-C.
53|3. WP-F only after A+B+C deployed and E merged, with explicit human permission; user
54|   pre-approved dummy-entry purging only — runner restarts must be recommended, not executed.
55|4. WP-G only after WP-F verification shows healthy discovery, pending the human dispatch decision.
